hints: In normal Nim, a player may remove any positive number of stones from one pile.
Compute the bitwise XOR of all pile sizes.
A zero XOR position is losing for the player to move; nonzero is winning.
analogy: If pile sizes have a nonzero XOR, choose one pile to make the combined XOR zero.
example: Piles 3,4,5 have XOR 3^4^5=2, so the first player can win.
algorithm: XOR every pile. Print the winner according to whether the result is zero.
correctness: When XOR is zero, every move changes it to nonzero; from nonzero, a move can reduce a pile to make XOR zero, so optimal play alternates into losing positions.
complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
